caption: This was the largest spy ring in American history
video_overlay_text_observed: Talking head over burned-in captions ("THE ISRAELI ART STUDENTS", "ISRAELI ART STUDENTS SETTING EXPLOSIVES?"); lower half shows photographs from Gelitin's book of the boxed-in 91st-floor studio.
audio_content_summary: Speaker describes the Israeli "art students" episode as an intelligence operation, then identifies the Austrian collective Gelitin as Israeli, reads the cardboard boxes in their 91st-floor World Trade Center studio as thousands of Littelfuse "BB-18" fuse holders for remote-controlled demolition, and says roughly 140 of those arrested were sent back to Israel without charges through Michael Chertoff.
implied_frame: Framing: an Israeli operation placed demolition charges in the towers under cover of an art residency. Documented separately and carried here: the DEA's June 2001 report on Israeli nationals posing as art students, and the Gelitin installation itself. Corrected here: Gelitin is an Austrian collective of four named artists holding a Lower Manhattan Cultural Council lease, and the boxes in its photographs were stacked as camouflage for the concealed balcony. Not supported by any source: that the boxes held fuse holders or any electrical component, that the collective was Israeli or connected to the DEA report, or that Michael Chertoff arranged the deportations — that last is asserted on advocacy sites and appears in no document, including our own copy of the Epstein release, where his eleven mentions are unrelated news clippings.
